claims.head: The Kings will send Gustafsson and Clarke at Pinto
claims.call: The Kings’ P1 (Gustafsson and Clarke) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Senators’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Kings keep sending Gustafsson and Clarke out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter Laviolette has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ third lines. Tonight the Senators’ third line is Greig, Pinto and Amadio.

claims.body: On physicality, Ottawa is near the top of the league, but Los Angeles is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Senators.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 23% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Thomas Chabot is out 1-2 weeks (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Tyler Kleven has taken his spot beside Jordan Spence.
William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 7 games.
Artem Zub was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Jake Sanderson.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 4% last season.
Kevin Fiala is on injured reserve (lower-leg surgery) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Alex Turcotte is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Quinton Byfield is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Alex Laferriere has taken his spot beside Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin.
Jared Wright was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Joel Armia and Scott Laughton.
Jared Wright was added to the roster on Oct 22 and has played beside Joel Armia and Scott Laughton.

LAK.head: A slightly uphill night for the Kings
LAK.body: Even though Los Angeles has home-ice advantage, Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents lately, and the Kings may be without Byfield. The Kings can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.

OTT.head: The Senators start a half-step ahead
OTT.body: Even though Los Angeles has home-ice advantage, Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents lately, and the Kings may be without Byfield. Still, it’s close: the Kings can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

items.text: The Senators are newly without Linus Ullmark and Thomas Chabot, and have been without William Eklund since Oct 8. Samuel Ersson is expected to start.
Artemi Panarin has a point in eight straight games against Ottawa, and 14 points in his last eight against them.
The Kings are newly without Quinton Byfield, have been without Alex Turcotte since Oct 6, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season.
Jordan Spence faces his old team, Los Angeles.
